text.p: These are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- The opposition parties will move an accountability bill in the Senate on Saturday and try to avenge their defeat in the National Assembly on a similar legislation three days ago.

- President Farooq Leghari will undertake a three-day visit to Uzbekistan on October 18 to discuss bilateral, regional and international issues with a particular reference to the new situation in Afghanistan. He will fly back home on October 20 and leave for Kyrgystan and Kazakhstan on October 25 on a five-day visit. He will return to Islamabad on October 30.
THE NATION

- The future of the much-awaited second tranche from the $600 million International Monetary Fund standby loan depends largely on the IMF's opinion on Pakistan's request for time to levy farm tax and cut defence budget irrespective of internal political scenario and regional security situation.

- An opposition delegation, in its meeting with President Farooq Leghari on Sunday, will take up the prevailing economic crisis, the IMF warning, the evasive attitude of the government towards the establishment of an accountability commission and extra-judicial killings in the country, Begum Abida Hussain said on Friday in Lahore.

- National Assembly Speaker Yousaf Raza Gillani told reporters in Multan on Friday that there seemed to be a consensus in the Assembly on the president's message sent to him for the adoption of a law to combat corruption.

- Malik Saeed Hassan, chairman of the newly appointed commission of inquiry to identify big loan defaulters, said in Lahore on Friday the commission would aim at giving a fool-proof system against the swallowing of billions of rupees from the national exchequer by the big fish.
DAWN
- Senior Pakistani economic officials will head for Washington next week to discuss an emergency economic package with the IMF, sources said.
- National Assembly (lower house) Speaker Yousaf Raza Gillani said on Friday he saw no possibility of military intervention in the country's political affairs.
- The National Assembly (lower house) will start its fourth parliamentary year with the president's address to a joint sitting of the two houses of parliament in the first week of November.

- Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar has said charges of human rights violations against Taleban, the new occupants of Kabul, were mere propaganda and that Afghanistan had experienced peace after Taleban took Kabul.
THE MUSLIM
- The federal cabinet will meet in Islamabad on Sunday under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto to consider and finalise a proposed accountability bill.

- Ghinva Bhutto, widow of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's slain brother Murtaza Bhutto, has finally decided to enter politics and head her husband's breakaway Shaheed Bhutto group of the Pakistan People's Party.
THE FRONTIER POST

- The government may give a surprise to opposition parties by promulgating an ordinance envisaging the constitution of an accountability commission mainly on the lines suggested in a bill presented by opposition leader Nawaz Sharif in the National Assembly last week.

- In a bid to muster support against Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government, Pakistan Muslim League party chief Nawaz Sharif will meet leaders of the newly formed independent parliamentary group next week.
BUSIESS RECORDER

- Two mutual funds worth over half a billion rupees, of Bears Stearns and State Life Insurance Corporation, in collaboration with Beg Associates, are waiting for a goahead signal from the Corporate Law Authority.

- The Terms Finance Certificate of ICI Pakistan was over-subscribed by nearly 50 percent, surpassing the general expectations of 30 to 40 percernt, and the issue of 250 million rupees fetched the ICI around 374.810 million.
- Trade volume between Pakistan and Uganda has shown an increase of 68.2 percent during last year, which underscores the real trade potential existing between the two sides.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
